column2: The people of [Root.GetName] have lived long under [Root.Owner.GetTitledName] and lords of [Root.Owner.GetHerHis] kind. Their children speak the tongue of the keep, marry its soldiers and keep its feast days. The old ways of the province are fading into songs the grandmothers sing.

Settlers from the homeland have come to [Root.GetName] in their hundreds: younger sons hungry for land, veterans of the conquest and their families, priests of our own gods. Within a generation they outnumber the old inhabitants, and the capital speaks our tongue.

[From.GetTitledName] has taken up the dress, the tongue and the customs of the foreigners at [From.Capital.GetName]. It seems my liege has forgotten where [From.GetHerHis] blood comes from, and who carried [From.GetHerHim] to power.
[From.GetTitledName] has given up the ways of the tribe. The chieftain's hall has become a proper keep, the war-band a household of knights and stewards.
